## Read the data
```{r read data}
con = DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "C:/Users/elite/OneDrive/School/ISA401/business_intelligence/Data/midwest_airbnb_extended/midwest_airbnb_extended.db")
listings     = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "listings") |> tibble::as_tibble()
availability = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "availability_monthly") |> tibble::as_tibble()
reviews      = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "reviews_monthly") |> tibble::as_tibble()
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
```


## Task 1
```{r Task 1}
# Count listings per host
host_count = listings |> 
  dplyr::count(host_id, name = "total_listings")

#Add count back to listings
listings_joined = listings |> 
  dplyr::left_join(host_count, by = "host_id")

#[A1]
listings_joined |> 
dplyr::filter(total_listings >= 10) |> 
dplyr::distinct(host_id) |> 
dplyr::count()

#[A2] 
listings_joined |> 
  dplyr::filter(city == "Chicago") |> 
  dplyr::summarize(
    total_chicago_listings = dplyr::n(),
    top_hosts_chicago = sum(total_listings >= 10),
    percent_held_by_top = (top_hosts_chicago / total_chicago_listings) * 100
      
  )
```

## Task 2
```{r task2}
listings |> 
  dplyr::filter(
    room_type == "Entire home/apt",
    accommodates >= 4,
    number_of_reviews >= 10,
    review_scores_rating >= 4.8
) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(price_per_person = price / accommodates) |> 
  dplyr::group_by(city, neighbourhood) |> 
  dplyr::summarize(
    median_ppp = median(price_per_person, na.rm = TRUE),
    qualifying_listings = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |> 
  dplyr::filter(qualifying_listings >= 20, city == "Columbus") |> 
  # [A3]
  dplyr::arrange(median_ppp)
  
```

## Task 3
```{r task3}
listings |> 
  dplyr::group_by(city, room_type) |> 
  dplyr::summarize(
    dplyr::across(
      c(price, reviews_per_month, estimated_revenue_l365d), 
      ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |> 
  # [A4]
  dplyr::filter(city == "Twin Cities", room_type == "Entire home/apt")
```


## Task 4
```{r task 4}
listings |> 
  dplyr::group_by(city) |> 
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(estimated_revenue_l365d), .by_group = TRUE) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    rank = dplyr::row_number(),
    # Mark rows that fall in the top 10%
    is_top_10 = rank <= ceiling(0.10 * dplyr::n())
  ) |> 
  dplyr::summarize(
    total_rev = sum(estimated_revenue_l365d, na.rm = TRUE),
    top_10_rev = sum(estimated_revenue_l365d[is_top_10], na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_top_10 = (top_10_rev / total_rev) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |> 
  # [A5]
  dplyr::filter(city == "Columbus")
```

## Task 5
```{r Task5}
oct_2026_avail <- availability |> 
  dplyr::filter(month == "2026-10")

listings |> 
  dplyr::filter(room_type == "Entire home/apt") |> 
  dplyr::inner_join(oct_2026_avail, by = "id") |> 
  dplyr::mutate(mostly_taken = nights_available < (0.5 * nights_in_month)) |> 
  dplyr::group_by(city) |> 
  dplyr::summarize(
    total_homes = dplyr::n(),
    taken_homes = sum(mostly_taken, na.rm = TRUE),
    share_mostly_taken = taken_homes / total_homes,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |> 
  # [A6 & A7]
  dplyr::arrange(share_mostly_taken)
```

## Task 6
```{r task6}
tc_demand = listings |> 
  dplyr::inner_join(reviews, by = "id") |> 
  dplyr::filter(month >= '2025-07', month <= '2026-06', city == 'Twin Cities') |> 
  dplyr::group_by(month) |> 
  dplyr::summarize(total_reviews = sum(reviews, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  # [A8]
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(total_reviews))
# [A9]
busiest_reviews <- max(tc_demand$total_reviews)
quietest_reviews <- min(tc_demand$total_reviews)
busiest_reviews / quietest_reviews
```


## Task 7
```{r task 7}
listings |> 
  dplyr::filter(room_type == "Entire home/apt", host_is_superhost %in% c("t", "f")) |> 
  dplyr::group_by(city, host_is_superhost) |> 
  dplyr::summarize(
    median_price = median(price, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_rating = median(review_scores_rating, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |> 
  # Widening the data so we can easily subtract the two columns
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    id_cols = city, 
    names_from = host_is_superhost, 
    values_from = c(median_price, median_rating)
  ) |> 
  # [B1]
  dplyr::mutate(premium = median_price_t - median_price_f)
```


## Task 8
```{r task8}
# [A10]
listings |> 
  dplyr::anti_join(availability, by = "id") |> 
  dplyr::group_by(city) |> 
  dplyr::summarize(lost_listings = dplyr::n()) |> 
  # Sort descending to easily see which city lost the most for your README
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(lost_listings))
```
